abstract: While sex differences in gene expression are increasingly recognized, how these differences emerge during prenatal development remains poorly understood. Now, Amlan Jyoti Naskar, Srimonta Gayen and colleagues use single-cell transcriptomic analysis to provide a valuable atlas of sex-biased gene expression and dosage compensation across mouse and human prenatal development. This atlas provides many insights into sex-differences in gene expression, including that sex-biased genes originate from both autosomal as well as sex chromosomes. To learn more about this work and the people behind it, we spoke to first author Amlan Jyoti Naskar and corresponding author Srimonta Gayen, Associate Professor in the Department of Developmental Biology and Genetics at the Indian Institute of Science in Bengaluru.
